Marathon Petroleum has climbed 8.23% over two weeks, with today's modest 0.18% gain capping a four-day rally that pushed the stock from $363.54 to $387.71. The sharp move reflects a combination of rising oil prices—U.S. crude has gained more than 9% this week amid escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions, including Iranian missile strikes on Kuwait this week—and near-maximum refinery utilization at 98%, which boosts margins for refiners when crude costs rise and fuel demand remains strong.

The geopolitical flare-up in the Middle East, particularly around the strategic Hormuz Strait region, has created supply uncertainty that typically lifts energy prices and benefits refiners. With refineries running hot and oil storage relatively contained at 711 million barrels, the refining business is operating in a tight, profitable window.
